title: "Dimensionality Reduction"
description: "The transformation of data into a lower-dimensional representation."
term: "Dimensionality Reduction"
letter: "D"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Dimensionality reduction represents data using fewer features or
coordinates. It can make data easier to visualize, store, process, or use
in a model.

## Technical explanation

Methods include feature selection, linear projections such as principal
component analysis, and nonlinear embeddings such as manifold-learning
methods. A reduced representation may preserve variance, distances, or
task-relevant information, depending on the method and objective.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Reducing dimensions can lower computational cost, help with visualization,
or address redundant features. However, important information may be lost,
and a visualization may distort distances or cluster structure.

## How it works

An algorithm selects a subset of features or learns a mapping
$f:\mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^k$ with $k<d$. The mapping is fit
on training data and applied consistently to new examples. The preserved
properties and limitations should be checked for the downstream task.

## Practical example

A team can project high-dimensional image embeddings to two dimensions
for exploratory visualization, then use the original or a separately
validated representation for production predictions.

## Common misconceptions

- A two-dimensional plot is not a faithful map of all high-dimensional
  distances.
- Dimensionality reduction does not guarantee better model accuracy.
- Fitting a reduction method before the train/test split can leak
  information from evaluation data.
